ideas.title: Why the Elephant's Trunk Has 40,000 Muscles #Shorts
ideas.concept: Reveal how thousands of tiny muscles let an elephant trunk pick up a single blade of grass, pull down branches, and drink without bones.
ideas.hook: An elephant trunk has no bones, but it can lift a tree branch and pick up one blade of grass.
ideas.keyVisual: Real elephant close-up using its trunk to pluck grass and curl around a branch, with a tight detail of the trunk tip and a wide herd shot.

ideas.title: Why the Ostrich Runs on Only Two Toes #Shorts
ideas.concept: Explain how an ostrich foot uses two specialized toes and a powerful tendon to stay balanced and sprint across open ground.
ideas.hook: This giant bird runs on just two toes, and one of them works like a spring.
ideas.keyVisual: Real ostrich sprinting across a savanna, followed by close footage of its two-toed foot striking the ground and a side profile of the running bird.

ideas.title: Why the Sea Turtle Finds the Beach Where It Was Born #Shorts
ideas.concept: Show how a sea turtle uses Earth's magnetic field like a map to navigate across the ocean and return to its nesting beach.
ideas.hook: After years in the open ocean, this turtle can find the exact beach where it hatched.
ideas.keyVisual: Real sea turtle swimming over open water, underwater navigation footage, and a nesting turtle moving up a moonlit beach toward the sand.
